chunks.rationale: electron/runner.js respondPermission is the load-bearing seam: updatedCommand is merged into updatedInput (command/cmd/script only), empty edits throw before splice so the prompt stays pending, and allowAlways after an edit emits addRules.ruleContent for the *edited* prefix via sessionAllowRule. Unedited Accept all still whole-tools, which is #479's job.
risks: Claude's npm build:* glob also matches npm build && rm -rf. Prefix matching is the CLI contract; this ticket only promises the glob is derived from the edited command, not the original.
updatedCommand on a non-command tool (Edit/Write) is ignored — an inbox that sent it anyway would silently approve the original JSON.

chunks.rationale: Pure helpers so #479 can reuse commandPrefix / sessionAllowRule without scraping runner.js. extractCommand is also what getPendingPermission exposes as pending.command.
risks: TWO_TOKEN_BINS is a denylist-of-sorts: python script.py becomes python:*, which is broader than npm test:*. Intentional; #479 can tighten the default glob UI later.

chunks.rationale: Replaces the inline <pre> card. Command-bearing tools get a textarea; others keep the JSON preview. Accept/Accept all send the field value; Reset restores; empty disables allow. Named so #291 can extract it later — QuestionPrompt/PlanPrompt still live in this file too.
risks: Always passing updatedCommand (even when unchanged) is load-bearing for 'what you see is what runs'; the runner treats trim-equal as not edited so audit text and session rules stay on the unedited path.
No autoFocus: a follow-up in the composer should not lose the caret when a permission appears.

chunks.rationale: PendingPermissionInfo.command and respondPermission.updatedCommand are the inbox contract (#291). The selected-thread hook just forwards the new field; a future inbox can call api.threads.respondPermission with any threadId.
risks: Older renderers that omit command still get a read-only JSON card (command == null).

chunks.rationale: permissionCommand.test.js covers extract/apply/prefix/session-rule. permissionPrompt.test.tsx covers edit, reset, empty, non-command tools. claude.test.js drives the fake CLI: edited allow, edited allowAlways prefix, empty does not consume the prompt. Existing unedited allowAlways still asserts whole-tool.
risks: The fake CLI permission scenario always proposes npm test; compound-command originals (rm -rf dist && npm build) are only covered in the renderer test.
Wand rewrite (NL edit via a fast model) is explicitly out of v1.
Unedited Accept all is still whole-tool Bash; do not treat this PR as shipping #479.
Guardrails are not re-run on the edited command — a user who edits ls into rm -rf / is approving it on purpose.
